texts: Cut not the thread of any life, for what you sever your hand cannot mend.
My cousin laughed as she crushed a spider hanging on its thread, and I went quiet, wondering whether any life should be taken so lightly.
doha on not hurting small creatures, thread of life
Compose a doha about the fragile thread that holds every living creature to life, from the smallest insect to the largest beast, and about how one who respects it will never cause pain to any being.
thread of life, no harm
doha on an elephant and a bell, being gentle with big animals
The elephant walks to the sound of the bell, mighty yet gentle; strength that harms none is the truest.
Please write a doha about the elephant who carries great strength and yet never hurts a creature, and the bell that calls to prayer, showing that real devotion means harming no living being.
elephant, bell, no cruelty
I saw a mahout beat his elephant while the bell for evening prayer was ringing, and I thought what kind of prayer is that.
The heron stands in holy stillness yet waits to take a life; what is the use of piety that kills?
doha on heron and traveler, pretending to be holy while killing
A traveler I met on the road prayed loudly at every halt, but ate the flesh of every creature he could find, and I wondered about his devotion.
heron, traveler, no killing
Compose a doha about the heron who stands as if in prayer, waiting to seize a living creature, and the traveler who prays but kills, showing that holiness without mercy for life is only a pretence.
doha on moneylender who is kind to animals but cruel to people, arrow
moneylender, arrow, no harm

Write a doha about the hunter who shoots an arrow at an innocent deer and the moneylender who gives to the poor but ignores the creatures that suffer, showing that true mercy extends to all that breathe.
The arrow flies, the animal falls; the moneylender gives alms but spares not the weak creature.
A moneylender in our town feeds the poor but organises hunting trips with his friends, and I would like him to hear a verse about it.
do not kill animals
The life in you is the life in every creature; to harm another is to wound your own self.
My daughter refused to eat meat after she saw how the chicken was killed, and I was moved by her sensitivity.
doha on why ppl shouldnt eat meat
Please write a doha about how the same life breathes in all creatures, and how the person who knows this cannot bring himself to kill a living thing for his own appetite or pleasure.
Compose a doha about the cruelty of killing an innocent animal merely for the pleasure of eating, and how the one who does so carries the pain of that creature into his own future.
At the festival they slaughtered a goat in front of everybody, and the way it looked at us stayed in my mind for weeks.
doha on animal sacrifice being wrong
Whose cry goes unheard when the innocent is led to sacrifice? Remember it is a life, as yours is.
mercy to animals
The net is cast and the innocent are caught; what pleasure has he who takes life for sport?
net, cruelty to creatures
Write a doha about the hunter's net which traps small birds and animals that have done no harm, and about how the one who weaves it traps his own soul in the cycle of cruelty and suffering.
doha on traps and nets cruelty
Some men in our area set a net for birds to sell and eat them, and I could not sleep after seeing the helpless creatures struggling.
My grandfather never harmed even an ant and used to carry insects out of the room gently, and I try to follow his example.
harm no creature
He who spares the smallest life is greater than he who conquers a thousand lands.
doha on compassion to insects

Please write a doha about how the person who is careful not to harm even the smallest of creatures has learnt the deepest lesson of religion, and about how his gentleness blesses all who live near him.
The moneylender sold seeds to farmers and then insisted on killing every bird that ate them, and I wished for a verse about leaving them in peace.
doha on seeds and birds, share with creatures
Sow your seed for all who hunger, bird and beast alike; the harvest of mercy is richest.

Write a doha about how a farmer who sows his seed should leave a share for the birds and the animals that also need to eat, rather than killing them, since all living things have a claim on the harvest.
seed, moneylender, no harm
swan, door, gentleness
doha on a swan at the door, never hurt a guest creature
The swan comes to the door of the kind and leaves unharmed; peace is the shelter of the gentle.
A swan wandered up to our door one evening, and my father shooed away the neighbour's boys who wanted to throw things at it.
Compose a doha about the swan that comes to a stranger's door seeking shelter, and about how the person who protects rather than harms it has shown the very meaning of kindness to all life.
The parrot held captive and the fly on the wall each hold a life as dear as yours; spare them.
doha on a parrot and a fly, all lives matter
Please write a doha about the parrot kept for amusement and the fly swatted in annoyance, to remind us that each life holds the same fear of death as our own, and no creature is too small for mercy.
My brother keeps a parrot and swats every fly without a thought, and I told him all lives are as precious to themselves as his is to him.
parrot, fly, spare them
doha on not eating meat, been vegetarian for a year
I stopped eating meat after I visited a farm and heard the animals cry, and now I eat in peace.
Write a doha about the person who gives up eating flesh out of pity for the animals, and about how his table becomes a place of peace where no creature has suffered for his pleasure.
no flesh, no cruelty
Where no creature cried for the meal, the meal itself is blessed.
doha on a lion and a thread: even a king of beasts should be gentle
lion, thread, mercy
Compose a doha about how even the lion, king of beasts, could hold his claws if he realised that life hangs by a thread for every creature, and about how humans, who can reason, should do much more.
A lion at the zoo paced in his small space, and I realised that all life hangs by a thread and that even a lion deserves freedom.
The lion's claws could spare, the thread of life is thin; teach, O Lord, the mighty to be gentle.
The inn near the old bus stand serves roasted meat to travellers, and I felt sick thinking of the ashes of those who died and the ashes of the animals killed.
inn, ash, no killing
Write a doha about the inn that serves the flesh of slaughtered animals to its guests, and about the ash that is the end of both man and beast, showing that all life returns to the same dust.
doha on inn serving meat, ash is the end for everyone
Both man and beast end as ash; why then, O host, do you serve one to the other?

Compose a doha about the crow who steals and the thief who steals, and the man who kills the crow in anger, showing that violence answers nothing and hurting a creature for a petty fault is the greater wrong.
doha on killing a crow for stealing, just wrong
A thief stole from our neighbour and the crowd beat him half to death, and the same people threw sticks at the crows that came, and it was dreadful to watch.
crow, thief, no violence
The crow takes a crumb and is stoned; the thief takes a purse and is beaten; where is mercy in any of this?
doha on being gentle toward every living thing
My child asked why we shouldn't step on ants, and I tried to explain that every creature has its own small life.
Walk gently on the earth, for beneath your feet are lives as dear to themselves as yours.

Please write a doha about the gentle person who walks the earth without trampling the small, speaks without wounding the weak and eats without taking life, showing that such a life is a continuous prayer.
no harm, no cruelty
stop animal cruelty
doha on people who beat their animals
The blows you give your servant beast return in kind; every blow is a debt unpaid.
My neighbour whips his bullock daily to make it pull a heavier load, and it breaks my heart to watch.
Compose a doha about the carter who beats the oxen that pull his load and calls it work, showing that cruelty to a voiceless creature is a sin that follows the doer through the years.
Compose a doha about sandalwood, which perfumes even the axe that cuts it and harms no creature, and about how the gentle person too gives fragrance to the world by refusing to harm any living being.
sandalwood, no harm
Sandalwood harms none, perfumes all; let me too live and leave a fragrance of mercy.
My uncle spent his life carrying injured animals to the shelter and his gentle ways were as fragrant as sandalwood for everyone.
doha on being gentle like sandalwood, hurting none
When the helpless are slaughtered, the Lord weeps; those who feast upon their flesh eat the tears of mercy.
At my cousin's wedding, a dozen goats were killed for the feast, and the bleating still echoes in my mind.

Please write a doha about the guilt of those who feast upon animals killed for their pleasure, and about how food obtained without cruelty is the only food that nourishes both the body and the spirit.
doha on killing animals for feasts
no blood on our plate
cage, free the birds
The cage may be gilded, yet the captive sings only of the sky; set him free, and be free yourself.
Write a doha about how every creature kept in a cage for the entertainment of others pines for the open sky, and how one who sets it free earns a blessing greater than any pilgrimage.
doha on freeing caged animals
I bought a caged bird at the fair just to set it free, and its first flight made me happier than I've been in months.
Compose a doha about the bitter gourd that hurts no creature and the rainbird that thirsts for rain, to teach that simple, bloodless food and a gentle nature make for a life that harms no one.
doha on bitter gourd diet and rainbird, living without harm
The rainbird drinks only clean rain and the bitter gourd harms no life; let simple food keep us gentle.
bitter gourd, rainbird, mercy
My grandmother grows bitter gourd and eats only what grows from the earth, and the rainbird that visits her garden is never driven away.
The lotus pond had a fisherman who netted every creature in it, and the pond, once alive with fish and flowers, was soon empty.
The lotus blooms where the fish may swim in peace; a pond emptied by cruelty bears no flowers.
doha on lotus and fish, killing fish ruins the pond
lotus, fish, spare them
Write a doha about the lotus pond where fish swim without fear and the fisherman who empties it with his traps, showing that the one who destroys life destroys also the beauty and peace around him.
Compose a doha about how a snake, though feared and driven away, takes life only when it is in danger, whereas man kills for pleasure and appetite, and the wise know which is the greater danger.
We found a snake in the courtyard and my father moved it gently away with a stick instead of killing it, saying it has as much right to live as we do.
snake, spare the creature
The snake bites in fear but man kills for pleasure; judge, O Lord, which is the cruel one.
doha on not killing snakes
The traveler who kills for his meal on the road has eaten his journey's reward; spare the life and gain the road.
A traveler stopped at our village, killed a hen for his supper, and I asked him how a person who walks the road to God can stain his hands with blood.
Please write a doha about the traveler who kills along the way for his meal, and how the weight of every life taken adds to the burden he must carry to the end of his journey.
doha for a traveler who eats meat on pilgrimage
traveler, spare the life
Compose a doha about the physician who heals the sick but kills animals to prepare medicines, and how the thread of one life cannot be cut to lengthen another, for all are bound by mercy.
The physician cuts a thread of life to mend another; is that healing, or only the shifting of pain?
The physician my family goes to makes medicines from the bodies of animals, and I've been wondering whether a cure that costs another life is any cure at all.
physician, thread, no killing
doha on animal-based medicine, no harm
doha on weaver's loom and silk, silkworms get killed
The silk weaver at his loom told me proudly how many worms are killed in making each saree, and I was horrified by the cost of beauty.
Please write a doha about the weaver whose loom makes beautiful cloth at the price of countless tiny lives, and about how true beauty is that which is woven without cruelty to any living being.
The loom weaves beauty, but if a life is the price, the beauty is a burden on the weaver's soul.
loom, silk, no cruelty
The net that takes the life of the free is woven of sin; cast it away and weave kindness instead.
Compose a doha about the net spread by the hunter to capture innocent creatures, and about how his trap is first of all a trap for his own soul, which cannot escape the consequence of its deeds.
doha on hunters setting nets
Poachers set nets in the wetlands near our village, catching all kinds of birds, and a friend and I broke them open at night.
net, spare the innocent
doha on a mountain, a mullah, not hurting animals for festival
From the mountain the cleric's call goes out; may it carry mercy to the creatures that suffer on festival day.
On the festival day, the cleric near our mountain village preached against killing animals unnecessarily, and many in the congregation listened.
Compose a doha about the cleric who tells his people from the mountain slope that sacrificing animals does not please God, because the Merciful One cherishes every living creature he has made.
mountain, cleric, no sacrifice

Please write a doha about the one-string lute whose single note stays in tune with all living things, and how the one who plays it with a gentle heart will never hurt another creature even in thought, word or deed.
My music teacher plays the one-string lute and will not even swat a mosquito, saying the same breath is in all.
doha on gentle musician who doesn't hurt anything
lute, gentle to all
One string, one note, one breath in all that lives; let not my hand silence another's song.

Compose a doha about the elephant, who is hunted for his tusks and chained for display, and about the cruelty of man who destroys such a noble being, showing that mercy is the sign of true strength and nobility.
elephant, hurt not
doha on being kind to elephants
The elephant in chains remembers the open land; free him, and you will be freed from your own cruelty.
I saw a chained elephant at a fair, swaying in distress, and I wished I could say something to all who passed it by.
doha on a tilak wearing man who eats meat and still calls himself holy
Please write a doha about the man with a sacred forehead mark who churns butter at dawn but eats meat at night, showing that religion lies in mercy toward all living beings, not in marks and rituals.
The mark on the brow, the churn at dawn, but blood on the plate by night; is that devotion?
forehead mark, churn, mercy
My uncle wears a big tilak and churns butter every morning but cannot go a day without meat, and I have long wondered how he squares it.
The peacock that wandered around our colony was hunted by some boys for the cremation ground feast, and I stopped them, shaking with anger.
doha on peacock killed for food, shamshan feast
peacock, cremation ground, spare life

Compose a doha about the peacock whose beauty delights all and who is hunted for a feast, and about the cremation ground where all feasts end, showing how foolish it is to take a life that cannot be restored.
The peacock dances in the rain and is hunted for the feast, yet the cremation ground awaits both hunter and prey.
Sandalwood gives fragrance to the axe, yet the sword takes lives for sport; which is the nobler path?
My grandfather, once a soldier, laid down his sword after the war and spent his later years planting sandalwood and saving injured animals.

Write a doha about the sword that takes life and the sandalwood that perfumes even the axe, to remind us that the noblest warrior is the one who puts down his weapon and uses his strength to protect the weak.
sword, sandalwood, mercy
doha on sandalwood and sword, peace beats war
Compose a doha about the elephant, gentle giant of the wild, and the swan who glides through the water harming none, showing how the strongest and most beautiful of beings live in peace with all.
The elephant and the swan harm none and are loved by all; such is the nobility of the gentle.
doha on elephant and swan being peaceful
elephant, swan, gentle ones
A swan and an elephant share the water at the sanctuary I visit, and I am always moved at how peacefully they coexist.

Please write a doha about the person who cannot bear to see any creature suffer, who will not take the life of even the smallest being, and who finds in that tenderness the heart of religion and peace.
I felt sick watching how the animals were treated at the slaughterhouse I passed on my way to work, and I have not eaten meat since.
doha on not eating animals, saw a slaughterhouse
hurt no living being
The one who feels the pain of the smallest creature has felt the pain of God.
The temple authorities in our town sacrifice a goat every year at the festival and say it pleases the deity, and I find it very hard to accept.
Write a doha showing that the Lord who lives in the temple cannot be pleased by the blood of an innocent animal, since He created and loves every creature, and true worship is gentleness toward all.
temple, no sacrifice
doha on animal sacrifice at the temple
The Lord who made the goat is not pleased by its blood; bring Him a heart that harms none.
doha on how an arrow hurts every living thing, hunting is cruel
arrow, mercy
Please write a doha about the arrow that flies from the hunter's bow and pierces an innocent creature without cause, and how the wounds it makes in the animal also wound the soul of the shooter.
My neighbour proudly hangs the heads of deer he shot with his bow on his wall, and every time I visit I feel uneasy.
The arrow wounds the deer, and the wound returns to the hunter's own heart.
doha on a thorn in the paw of an animal, helping not hurting
Compose a doha about the thorn that pierces the foot of a creature in the wild and the kind person who removes it gently, showing that a heart which feels the pain of another can never harm him.
The thorn that pricks the beast's foot pricks the heart of the kind; so dear is the creature to the tender.
I found a stray dog limping with a thorn in its paw and gently pulled it out, and the dog licked my hand, and I knew right then why I never wished to hurt any animal.
thorn, help the creature
From the boat I saw fishermen throwing back the small catches to die on the shore, and I felt sad for the dying creatures.
boat, no killing
Write a doha about the boat that sails across the water carrying traps, and the people on it who destroy the life of the waters for profit, showing that a seeker must cross life without harming it.
The boat crosses the water and leaves no wound; so should the seeker cross life, harming none.
doha on boat voyage harming no life

Compose a doha about the tortoise, which is hunted for its shell and sacrificed in temples, and about the temple that has forgotten mercy, showing that the place of worship is empty when cruelty is permitted inside.
The tortoise bears its shell upon its back, yet is slain at the temple; what god delights in such offerings?
At the temple near my aunt's village, a tortoise was killed as an offering, and the horrified child in me still cries about it.
doha on tortoise and temple, no sacrifice of animals
tortoise, temple, spare life
The priest preaches mercy in the morning and feasts on flesh at night; what is the worth of such a sermon?
The priest in our community gives talks about non-violence in the morning, but I saw him at a feast eating meat, and I lost faith.
doha on priest who preaches ahimsa but eats meat
priest, hypocrisy, no killing
Compose a doha about the priest who tells others to be kind to all creatures but eats the flesh of slaughtered animals himself, showing that true teaching must be lived, and not merely spoken aloud.

Please write a doha about the thief who steals a life from an innocent animal, and the one who steals goods from a neighbour, saying both are robbers, and the river of mercy cleanses neither until they repent.
The thief who broke into our shed was chased off, yet the same crowd killed a stray dog by the river that was only hungry and posed no harm.
doha on killing a hungry dog by the river, cruelty to creatures
thief, river, spare life
The thief of goods is hunted, the thief of lives goes free; the river of mercy asks for justice for both.
Every life holds the same breath as yours; to take it lightly is to scorn the Giver of breath.
respect all life

Write a doha about the breath that moves in every living being, which the wise recognise as the same in all, so that they cannot bring themselves to cause pain to another any more than they would to themselves.
doha on respecting all forms of life
After I watched my child hold a dying bird with such tenderness, I understood what it means to honour a life.
I tied a thread around a stray kitten's neck to lead it along, and my teacher told me that even gentle threads can hurt a creature that wants to run free.
The thread that binds a free creature binds also its keeper; let go, and you both shall breathe.

Compose a doha about the thread that ties a wild creature against its will, and how the person who respects the freedom of every living thing lets it go and finds the thread on his own heart loosening too.
doha on not tying up animals
thread, set them free
Write a doha about the date palm which gives sweet fruit and shade to all without killing anything, as an example of the gentle life that takes nothing from any creature and gives much to every one.
My grandmother lives off the dates and grains of her small land, never touching meat, and her life has been the gentlest I know.
The date palm gives its sweetness without taking a life; blessed is the table that is spread this way.
date palm, gentle food
doha on plant-based food and date palm, no killing
Compose a doha about how violence in word, thought or deed always returns to its source, and the person who has made peace with all living beings sleeps soundly, eats gently and dies without fear.
He who harms none fears none; his sleep is sweet and his death is gentle.
After I gave up hunting, a strange peace came over me, and I sleep better than I have in years.
doha on peace that comes from not harming anyone
harm none, fear none
doha on moth dying near a bulb, saving insects
Every night I carry out the moths that circle the glare so that they do not die in it, and my family teases me but I feel good.
Please write a doha about the moth that circles the glare and dies, and about how the compassionate person protects such little lives, knowing that no being is too small to be loved by the Creator.
The moth flies to the glare and dies, and the kind hand lifts it away; blessed is the hand.
moth, spare small lives
fish, water pot, spare life
doha on a fish in a water pot, set it free
Write a doha about the fish kept in a pot of water for display, which longs for open water, and how the kind person lets it go and frees himself from the guilt of keeping a free being captive.
The fish in the pot of water dreams of the open stream; set it free, and free your own soul.
My kids kept a fish in a pot of water in the kitchen, and when I explained how it suffers, they carried it to the stream and let it swim away.
The fly on the wall and the snake in the grass alike dread death; where is your mercy for them?
fly, snake, harm none
My mother never kills a fly or a snake that wanders into the courtyard, only gently shoos it away, and I try to do the same.
Compose a doha about the fly and the snake, creatures that are most often killed in fear or disgust, and how the person who has learnt gentleness spares them and lets them go on their way.
doha on not killing flies and snakes
The fish vendors near the harbour was full of dying creatures gasping for air, and as I walked past I felt I should say something.
fish, spare them
Please write a doha about the fish gasping for air on the vendor's table, and how the one who sees its struggle and turns away from eating it has learnt the most important lesson of compassion.
doha on fish gasping on the table, pity them
The fish gasps on dry land as you would gasp in water; feel its pain, and spare it.
